subject: Onboarding choreography: SCIM/SSO gating and ephemeral service accounts
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@enterpriseco.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@enterpriseco.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood onboarding kickoff — authz sequencing and constraints

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the intro last week. We're ready to kick off the onboarding sprint for EnterpriseCo. A few constraints up front: our security team requires SCIM provisioning with groups limited to two org units initially, SAML metadata exchanged before any cutover, and IP allowlist entries limited to a /29 per region. We also need ephemeral service account guidance for automation that runs reports against the Redwood API.

Before we lock dates, can you confirm:
- What artifacts you’ll need from us to validate SAML/SCIM?
- Whether Redwood supports time-limited service account keys or recommended rotation cadence out of the box?
- A suggested canary plan for IP allowlist cutover to avoid lockouts

We're aiming for a Nov 16 production go-live but flexible if you need extra runway. Attaching our baseline SAML metadata and current SCIM schema export.

Attachments: enterpriseco-saml-metadata.xml (SAML metadata), scim-schema.csv (current SCIM export)

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Identity & Integrations
EnterpriseCo
liam@enterpriseco.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding kickoff — authz sequencing and constraints

Liam — thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts, that helps a lot. High level responses inline below and a proposed mutual action plan attached (mvp-ma-plan.xlsx).

Quick answers:
- Artifacts: we need your SAML metadata (you attached — perfect), an assertion examples doc (IdP-initiated vs SP-initiated), SCIM sample payloads for user and group creates/updates (the CSV is a good start; we'll ask for JSON examples during engineering sync), and your IP ranges per region for the /29 allocation.
- Service accounts: Redwood supports short-lived API tokens for service accounts with rotation via our Console (recommended 24-72 hour rotation for automation). For longer-running CI workflows we recommend a delegated ephemeral token exchange; Ben will outline patterns below.
- Canary plan: we typically do a two-step cutover — staging allowlist with a proxy test range, then a single-customer production window with rollback script. We'll detail steps in the implementation checklist.

Proposed next steps (high level):
1) Week of Nov 9: technical working session (engineering pair) to validate SAML assertions and SCIM sample payloads.
2) Nov 11: implementation sprint kickoff (CS + Eng), provision staging IP /29 and service account templates.
3) Nov 16: soft go-live for subset (read-only traffic) -> monitor, then full production on Nov 18 if green.

I cc'd Monica (CS Ops) and Ben (Solutions Eng) so we can schedule the working session and confirm the engineering checklist. If you want to move the go-live earlier/later we can adapt but prefer to lock the Nov 11 kickoff as our baseline.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding kickoff — authz sequencing and constraints

Thanks, quick follow-up with concrete engineering patterns and the checklist we'll use in the working session.

Key technical notes:
- SAML: we've seen two common pitfalls — clock skew in assertion consumers and NameID format mismatches. Please include the IdP SSO URL, EntityID, and signing cert expiration in the payload samples you bring. We'll run a lightweight SP metadata validation during the call.
- SCIM: Redwood's provisioning uses SCIM 2.0 with support for Group -> Roles mapping. The scim-schema.csv maps fine but we need JSON create/update examples for: user create with externalId, group create with members array, and a delta update where a user is removed from a group. We'll share our sample payloads in the working session.
- Service accounts: recommended approach for your automation: create a short-lived service account (48h token) and a rotation Lambda that exchanges a long-lived credential (stored in your KMS) for a Redwood ephemeral token using our Token Exchange endpoint. We'll share pseudocode in the working session.

Canary/IP plan (for Nov 16):
- Provision a staging /29 in us-west-2 for smoke tests.
- Provision a production /29 and a proxy IP for the first production window.
- During cutover, keep the old auth path active and run traffic split 90/10 for 2 hours, check audit logs for 401s, then flip if green. We'll provide a rollback script that removes the production allowlist entry.

I've attached the MVP action plan and a short checklist we'll walk through on Nov 11.

Attachments: mvp-ma-plan.xlsx

On scheduling: I'm available Mon/Tue Nov 9-10 10am-2pm PT for the engineering pairing. Which slot works for your IdP engineer?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
